questions.q: A grid has n_estimators [50, 200], max_depth [3, 6, None] and min_samples_leaf [1, 5], with cv=5. How many model fits does GridSearchCV run during the search (before the final refit)?
questions.explain: 2 x 3 x 2 = 12 combinations, each cross-validated on 5 folds, giving 60 fits. The final refit adds one more.

questions.q: What does refit=True (the default) do in GridSearchCV?
options: Repeats the search until the score stops improving
Retrains the best combination on the whole training set and exposes it as best_estimator_
Refits the scaler on the test set
Removes the worst hyperparameters from the grid
questions.explain: After the search, GridSearchCV refits the top-ranked combination on all the training data so gs.predict works immediately.

questions.q: The best max_depth is None, the largest option in your grid. What should you do?
options: Nothing; the grid is guaranteed to contain the optimum
Consider widening or extending the grid, since the true best may lie beyond the edge
questions.explain: A winner at the edge suggests the optimum could lie outside the grid, so extend it and search again.

questions.q: How do you name a logistic regression's C in a param_grid when the pipeline step is called "clf"?
questions.explain: Pipeline parameters are addressed as step name, two underscores, parameter name.

questions.q: The top two grid results had mean F1 of 0.917 and 0.909 with standard deviations of 0.023 and 0.038. How should you interpret them?
options: They are close to a statistical tie, since the gap is smaller than the spread
The second is better because its std is larger
questions.explain: A gap of 0.008 is much smaller than the fold-to-fold standard deviations, so the search cannot reliably separate them.
